clue.text: A help for the latecomers?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that helps people who arrive late to an appointment
setter's reading: people who come to education late in life, or who study late in the day

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what might help people who always turn up late.
explanation.walkthrough: Latecomers here are adults returning to learning, and the help is classes held in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening classes serve adults who missed out on education earlier, so they help those coming late to learning.

clue.text: This fare's not overdone in France

definitions.text: This fare's not overdone in France

blocks.clueFragment: This fare's not overdone in France
blocks.note: surface reading: French food that is lightly cooked
setter's reading: a style of cooking known for small, delicate portions rather than heavy rich dishes

explanation.surface: A remark about how French cooks avoid overcooking their food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not overdone' points both to light cooking and to small, unfussy portions, the hallmark of the French style that rejected heavy classical sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: This modern French cookery style favours light sauces, fresh ingredients and small, artfully presented portions.

clue.text: Pull up Church from a deep split

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the word for pull is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to lug is to pull or haul
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a church out of a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gulch is a narrow, steep-sided ravine, a deep cleft in the land.

clue.text: Token ritual rearranged after time

indicators.note: things rearranged are put in a new order, so the word ritual is shuffled

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A ceremony gets reshuffled once time has passed, making it merely symbolic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After time' places the shuffled letters after T, so T comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something existing in name only, like a nominal head with no real power.

clue.text: Put in place in school?

blocks.note: surface reading: assigned a position or ranked
setter's reading: placed in a form or year group, the way pupils are grouped at school

explanation.surface: A pupil is told where to sit, or put firmly in their place, at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means categorised generally, and the question mark hints at its school sense of being placed in a teaching group.
explanation.definitionFit: To be categorised or ranked is to be assigned a position, as pupils are allotted to a form.

clue.text: Interested spectator to note runs

blocks.note: to note something is to remark or notice it
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A keen onlooker at a cricket match keeps note of the runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches attentively, without taking part, is a watcher or onlooker of events.

clue.text: One doesn't want to do this at a bank

definitions.text: One doesn't want to do this at a bank

blocks.note: surface reading: a slope, such as a riverbank, where one might trip and fall

blocks.clueFragment: One doesn't want to do this at a bank
blocks.note: setter's reading: a financial bank, where an account's funds could be lost

explanation.surface: Advice about keeping your footing on a steep riverside slope.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means toppling over, but at a financial bank the balance is the money in one's account.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple or stumble is the idiom, and at a financial institution it would mean money vanishing from an account.

clue.text: Assumes Parent-Teacher Association's do has a good mix

indicators.note: a good mix churns its ingredients thoroughly, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: PTA is the usual abbreviation, with the possessive S
taken as written; a do is a party

explanation.surface: A school fundraising party proves to be a good mix of people.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner or attitude is to take it up as one's own, just as one takes on a name or a cause.

clue.text: Say I'll be in the road or at sea

definitions.text: be in the road or at sea

blocks.clueFragment: Say I'll be in the road or at sea
blocks.note: surface reading: someone announcing they will be travelling, by road or by ship

blocks.clueFragment: in the road or at sea
blocks.note: setter's reading: something found in the middle of a street or surrounded by ocean, and 'Say I'll' hints at how the start is pronounced

explanation.surface: A traveller declares they will be either on the road or out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A traffic refuge in mid-road and a piece of land in the ocean share one name, whose first syllable is said like 'I'll'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both land surrounded by water and a raised refuge surrounded by traffic.

clue.text: Reservation about the French garment

indicators.note: a thing placed about another surrounds it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a reservation is a doubt or misgiving
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone has reservations about the French style of a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Renaissance Europe, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Helps in a way in Italian town, when one is lost

indicators.note: something lost goes missing, so a single letter standing for one drops out
one part is placed in the middle of the other, so it is surrounded

blocks.note: Assisi is the Umbrian hill town of St Francis
the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone finds their way around an Italian town after losing one of their party.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping one I from the town leaves ASSIS, and the street abbreviation goes in before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give aid or support, so the plural verb form matches helps.

clue.text: Eyes close to them? Hope sleep's improved

indicators.note: improving something reworks it into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone with tired eyes hopes their sleep gets better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eyes close' reads as falling asleep, but it describes spying eyes pressed up against small openings in a door.
explanation.definitionFit: Small holes in doors or walls are looked through with an eye placed right next to them.

clue.text: Port? Yes, overseas wine

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a famous Brazilian port
ja is German (and Dutch) for yes, a foreign word

explanation.surface: Someone accepts an offer of port and then a foreign wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, which helps the wine-drinking surface, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish table wine from the region of that name.

clue.text: Marketing cruise, we hear

indicators.note: something we hear is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: to cruise is to sail

explanation.surface: A holiday company advertises a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marketing' must be read as a noun-like activity: offering goods for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketing goods means putting them on offer to buyers, the business of selling.

clue.text: Attacking position for the game leader

blocks.note: bridge is a card game
a head is a leader or chief

explanation.surface: Someone takes an aggressive stance to become top of their game.
explanation.definitionFit: A military foothold won on the enemy's side of a river, from which an advance can be launched.

clue.text: Farm accommodation for females

blocks.note: surface reading: lodging for workers on a farm
setter's reading: female birds, the ones that lay eggs

explanation.surface: A farm offers lodgings reserved for women workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The females are poultry, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop where laying birds are kept on a farm is literally shelter for female chickens.

clue.text: Winning, or following?

blocks.note: first meaning: achieving success
second meaning: coming after, as one monarch takes over from another

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites us to choose, but the word means both.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is both to achieve one's aim and to come next in order, inheriting a role.

clue.text: Neat cross

blocks.note: first meaning: smart and stylish, as in a sharp dresser
second meaning: irritable and short-tempered

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat cross' looks like a tidy X, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both stylish smartness and a bad-tempered, curt manner of speaking.

clue.text: I love being in play in a model scene

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: An actor declares their love of performing in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional miniature of a scene, often shown in museums.

clue.text: It's essential to include Latin. Annoyed?

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: something essential is needed
L is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A pupil is irritated at being told Latin is compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or irritate them with persistent jibes.

clue.text: Encourage what a gambler has

blocks.note: taken as the article: a gambler has one of something
a gambler places a wager

explanation.surface: Someone asks what drives a gambler on.
explanation.walkthrough: What a gambler has is 'a bet', two words that run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or incite someone, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Fish around river-ditch

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word goes on both sides of the other

blocks.note: a tench is a freshwater fish
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A fish swims about where a river meets a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow excavation in the ground, as dug for drainage or by soldiers.

clue.text: An expression of contempt that's silly

blocks.note: the article
pish is an old exclamation of scorn

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at something foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving like an ape means acting foolishly or imitatively, hence silly.

clue.text: Exaggerate importance of cricketing worth?

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
worth is value

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a cricketer's worth is being inflated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricketing' supplies the cricket term for a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Rating something too highly means giving it more worth or significance than it merits.

clue.text: Wrongdoings when first three leave the armed forces

indicators.note: those leaving depart, so the opening three letters are taken away

blocks.note: the services are the army, navy and air force

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour follows when the top brass quit the military.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices are immoral habits or wicked conduct, in the plural like the definition.

clue.text: A half-ripe plum could be in flower

indicators.note: half keeps just the front portion of the word ripe
could be suggests the letters might turn into something else when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the first two of four letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plum not yet fully ripe might still be in blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: The primula is a genus of flowering plants that includes the primrose and cowslip.

clue.text: City's mathematical branch cut short, expressed briefly

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
conics, the study of conic sections, is a branch of geometry

explanation.surface: A city's mathematics department is trimmed, described in few words.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, after the terse Spartans of Laconia.

clue.text: Meriel leads ramble in the country

indicators.note: rambling wanders without a set route, so these letters stray into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A woman named Meriel heads a countryside walking group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' looks like rural land for the ramble, but it names a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a poetic nickname for Ireland, celebrated for its lush green landscape.
